content:
Tomorrow is Apple's most important annual product launch event, where new Apple Watch models are expected to be unveiled. In a surprising move, Apple has completely removed all configurations of the Apple Watch SE 3 from its official website.

Apple's official website displays "Currently Unavailable" for all Apple Watch SE 3 models.

Apple is widely expected to unveil new iPhone and Apple Watch models at its launch event on September 9, along with potentially other products such as AirPods.

However, on the eve of the event, one of the existing Apple Watch models—the Apple Watch SE 3—has already been pulled from sale on Apple's official website.

According to MacRumors, no matter how you configure any version of the Apple Watch SE 3, you will see the Apple website display the model as "Currently Unavailable" at the final step, whether choosing delivery options or in-store pickup at an Apple Store.

Apple generally does not clear inventory before a product is set to be replaced.

However, the most puzzling aspect this time is that there have been absolutely no rumors about an Apple Watch SE 4.

Instead, we are only expecting two new models: the Apple Watch Series 12 and the Ultra 4.

The current stock shortage could be a system glitch and may be resolved soon. However, as things stand, it seems to suggest that a next-generation model may debut tomorrow.

We will continue to provide updates on the latest availability status of the Apple Watch SE 3.
